paper_title: Constructing Doppelgängers of Greedy Geometric Spanners in Practice
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 4
statement: Despite the progress made by Shariful et al. in [32], practical construction of spanners which closely resemble greedy spanners in terms of average degree, weight, and degree, especially for low t-values (≤ 2), remains an open problem. Note that Delaunay triangulations are 1.998-spanners [35] with O(n) edges that can be constructed in O(n log n) time (in practice, takes a few seconds even for millions of points). So, constructing t-spanners with t around 2 or more is not considered challenging in practice.
context: Shariful et al. [32] recently observed that Bucketing is slow for large values of n. For instance, when n = 106 , t = 1.1, and the points are uniformly distributed inside a square, Bucketing took around five days to generate the spanner. So, they engineered a practical parallel algorithm Fast-Sparse-Spanner, that generated geometric graphs fast and had average degrees close to those of greedy spanners. Fast-Sparse-Spanner could generate a 1.1-spanner for the same above point set in just 55 minutes, making it much faster than Bucketing in practice. They experimentally observed that Fast-Sparse-Spanner consistently generated t-spanners across a wide variety of distributions and real-world point sets. To check for the t-spanner property, they also devised an auxiliary practical stretch factor measurement algorithm, named Fast-Stretch-Factor, since Fast-Sparse-Spanner is not theoretically guaranteed to generate t-spanners. However, the weights and degrees of the generated graphs are far from the actual greedy spanners owing to the presence of long WSPD spanner edges, which form a backbone of their spanners. Despite the average degree of the generated graphs being close to those generated by Bucketing (see Table 1), the degrees and lightness values substantially differed. For the point set used in Table 1, the degrees of graphs generated by Fast-Sparse-Spanner and Bucketing were 78 and 18, respectively, and the lightness values were 16.7196 and 11.0354, respectively. Despite the progress made by Shariful et al. in [32], practical construction of spanners which closely resemble greedy spanners in terms of average degree, weight, and degree, especially for low t-values (≤ 2), remains an open problem. Note that Delaunay triangulations are 1.998-spanners [35] with O(n) edges that can be constructed in O(n log n) time (in practice, takes a few seconds even for millions of points). So, constructing t-spanners with t around 2 or more is not considered challenging in practice. What are doppelgängers of greedy spanners? We introduce the notion of (a, b)- doppelgänger. A t-spanner H on a point set P is a (a, b)-doppelgänger of the greedy spanner G on P , if its average degree and lightness do not exceed those of G by more than additive constants a and b, respectively. Average degree and lightness are two central measures of spanner quality, and spanners with similar values for these metrics tend to be structurally similar. Thus, smaller values of a and b indicate better doppelgängers. Such doppelgängers are especially appealing to practitioners when they can be constructed significantly faster than the greedy spanner itself. The term “approximation” has not been used in this work intentionally, as the Approximate-Greedy [19] algorithm claims to generate spanners that are approximations of greedy spanners, but, in reality, they are structurally very different from the actual greedy spanners (also, see Table 1). Our contribution. Motivated by the lack of fast practical algorithm to generate (a, b)- doppelgängers of greedy spanners for low values of a and b, we design and engineer Θ-Greedy, a new spanner construction algorithm, based on Θ-Graph. We found Θ-Greedy to be considerably faster than our closest competitor Bucketing, and always produced high quality doppelgängers in our experiments. In our experiments, both a and b never exceeded 0.1. To our knowledge, no other known algorithm can achieve this while being fast and scalable in practice. See Figure 2 for a visual comparison between Θ-Greedy and Bucketing.
